description.narrative: Samarbetet med Council of Europe syftar till att stärka utbildningen i demokratiskt medborgarskap på grundval av Council of Europe normer och praxis. Målgrupperna är utbildningspolitiska beslutsfattare, lokalsamhällen, rektorer, lärare, elever och skolpersonal från utvalda grund- och gymnasieskolor i pilotsyfte. Delen av detta ingripande omfattar en omfattande granskning av utbildning i demokratiskt medborgarskap i Albanien för att identifiera möjligheter och utmaningar för att ytterligare anpassa den nationella läroplanen till Europarådets standarder och nationella politiska mål. Komponenten för demokratisk skolstyrning kommer att stödja 75 pilotskolor i att utveckla och genomföra politik och praxis för demokratisk styrning för att skapa en inkluderande och möjliggörande lärandemiljö för alla elever, med fokus på områden som digitalt medborgarskap, mediekompetens, säkerhet på nätet, bekämpning av mobbning, undervisning i kontroversiella frågor och klimatförändringar. Syftet med komponenten för lärarstöd är att förbättra lärarnas yrkesmässiga kompetenser, attityder och praxis genom e-lärande, regionalt kollegialt utbyte, utbildning och handledningsevenemang.

This cooperation with Council of Europe aims to strengthen democratic citizenship education based on Council of Europe standards and practices. The target groups are education policy makers, local communities, school principals, teachers, students and school staff from selected pilot primary and secondary schools. The Policy Support component of this intervention includes a comprehensive review of democratic citizenship education in Albania to identify the opportunities and challenges for further aligning the national curriculum to Council of Europe standards and national policy objectives. The Democratic School Governance component will support 75 pilot schools in developing and implementing democratic governance policies and practices to create an inclusive and enabling learning environment for all students, focusing on areas such as digital citizenship, media literacy, safety online, fighting bullying, teaching controversial issues, and climate change. The Teacher Support component aim at enhancing teachers’ professional competences, attitudes and practices through e-learning, regional peer exchange, training and coaching events.

The goal of the intervention is to improve quality of education in Albania by strengthening democratic citizenship education based on CoE standards and practices. Intermediate outcome is the following: The capacity of the Albanian education system to develop learners’ competences for a democratic culture, in line with national policy objectives and CoE instruments and approaches, is strengthened. Immediate outcomes are: 1. (Policy support) The policy and methodological framework on democratic citizenship education and the democratic governance of schools are aligned to key national education objectives and the Council of Europe standards and approaches. 2. (Democratic school governance) School children in selected schools are provided with the skills, knowledge and opportunities to participate in the decision-making processes in their schools and communities and engage in school and community-based projects jointly with civil society organisations. 3. (Teacher support) Teachers develop new professional competences, practices and attitudes that better contribute to the development of competences for democratic culture in learners and ensure an inclusive and enabling learning environment for all children.

title.narrative: Agreement Sida and Council of Europe

description.narrative:
- At the policy level, the project supported the implementation of the National Education Strategy by fostering a safe and supportive school environment. It contributed to the pilot implementation of the Council of Europes Education in Times of Emergencies and Crises (EDURES) toolkit in Albanian schools to enhance crisis preparedness and prioritise student well-being. Additionally, the project assisted the Aleksandër Xhuvani University in Elbasan in integrating human rights education into two teacher preparation programmes by introducing new courses on the subject.
- Student-led initiatives, including the 'Fake Fact Initiative,' 'Fighting Bullying in Schools,' and 'Human Rights Promotion, continued demonstrating a significant positive impact, driving improvements in key areas such as media literacy, democratic participation, and educational quality.
- The Democratic School Governance initiative strengthened the network of 75 schools across 23 Albanian cities. The project has worked on designing the model of 17 Democratic Culture Labs (DCLs) to be established in schools to promote democratic participation and critical thinking.
- When it comes to capacity building/ teacher support, the project trained 690 education professionals through face-to-face and online programmes, helping them develop competencies for democratic culture, inclusive education, and addressing bullying, violence, and extremism in schools. These efforts contributed to a more democratic and participatory learning environment, strengthening the overall educational system in Albania. Overall, the project contributed to the National Teacher Development Plan introduced by the Ministry of Education and Sports (MoES) in March 2024, focusing on professional development and quality education. - An example of this contribution is the following: Training modules have been adopted in the Albanian language, accredited by the Agency of Quality Assurance of Pre-University Education System and Trainings, and as recommended by the project team, are included in the teachers performance and teachers qualification process organised at the end of 2024 and the beginning of 2025. Moreover, training modules in the CoE's Lemon Platform are available to all Albanian teachers, promoting the approach of viewing EDC/HRE concepts through a more cross-curricular and interdisciplinary lens.
- The project launched the "Learning from the Past" initiative in partnership with the Authority for Information on Former State Security Documents (AIDSSH), which encouraged students to explore Albania's historical past and its implications for democratic values. Another significant initiative, "Never Violence," in collaboration with the Swedish Institute, promoted non-violent child- rearing practices. By November 2024, this initiative reached 500 students and educators, emphasizing a nurturing, rights-based environment for children. The project also empowered over 1690 students to combat bullying and violence in schools through student-led activities.
